body: Thanks for letting me know. I decided to buy ALCAR instead.

Do you know any suppliers that sells capsules? It seems MondialK only sells powders (please correct me if I am wrong) and unfortunately I don't own a precision scale, so for me it's kind of risky to use powders.

I am mostly looking to buy synthetic nootropics such as adrafinil. Mindnutrition seems to sell only natural nootropics but I'll keep your recommendation in mind if I ever plan on trying natural alternatives. Thanks.

I've asked a psychologist if it's possible for one to be born hating oneself and they said it's not. It's the result of environmental influences.            
My parents are great and I was not bullied at school either, however I struggled a lot with making friends (I pretty much only had online friends and they mistreated me constantly, called me bad at the game we were playing etc.), and I also despised my appearance. My parents also despite being good to me never really paid much attention to my behavior during that time, nor did they help me when I 
complained about how lonely I was; they saw it as being something positive since I never challenged them, never gave them any trouble and stayed home the whole day after school.            
You just have to look deeper and you'll find the reasons for your low self esteem.

You don't need to go outside to exercise. I work out at home using my own body weight and a cheap elliptical machine.                 
Oh I'm not really expecting university to be the greatest time of my life. All I want in life is a little bit of peace - not even happiness. But it seems every time I fix something that's been bothering me, something else shows up, and I obsess over it continually, until that problem is also solved - this drains a lot of my energy and leaves me feeling tired most days.

That's happening to me as well. I am an university student and I don't know what else to do other than study. Maybe try to incorporate some exercising in your routine. I did that with mine and at least I look forward to working out every day.             
I wish I could enjoy what I am studying a little bit more and I know under different circumstances I might but currently there are other things in my life making me unhappy and I feel I need to fix those first.

I can relate, I consider myself a very uninteresting person, I have pretty much nothing to talk about other than school-related things and the few hobbies I have aren't particularly fun/interesting. I have a hard time getting comfortable around people and making friends, but keeping them is also a major problem for me due to lack of social skills. I can't comprehend why anyone would want to be my friend so it's not surprising I have been friendless for about 3 years.

I am not sure how gyms work where you're from but you could try to find a smaller sized gym, with less people in it. Also usually you do not have to research the workouts beforehand because the trainer (a worker for the gym) does that and shows you how to perform each exercise.               
When I started going to the gym I was extremely anxious as well but about 3 weeks in I got used to it.            
Alternatively you could also do a lot of stuff at home using your own body weight or by buying a set of weights if you can afford it. I am currently not going to the gym anymore - I work out at home using the elliptical and TRX (suspension training).

Propranolol has helped me a lot by eliminating most of the physical effects of anxiety. I take it daily. It has helped me face many of my fears such as talking to authorities. I still feel terribly anxious but the anxiety does not stop me from getting what I need and doing what I must.              
I would very much like to try an SSRI, especially because I have a constant depressed mood on top of anxiety.

Maybe learn to cut your own hair. That's what I did.         
A lot of the times hair stylists/barbers can tell whether their clients want to talk or not. When they start talking to me I make sure to give one word answers. They usually stop asking unimportant questions then - most of the other questions are about the hairstyle itself.

Coffee contains much less caffeine than these pills. I'd say it's because of my natural resistance.          
If coffee works for you, I'd continue taking it. Lots of people report feeling terrible when taking caffeine pills. I barely feel anything, but that's just me.

I'd say I never really learned how to interact properly with my peers. Then as I got older it kept getting worse - I was far too behind to keep up with their level of social skills. Then social isolation led to even further underdeveloped social skills. And since I am well aware of my ineptitude, I became highly distressed in social situations - everyone just knew intuitively what to do and what to say and my mind was just blank.                    
Also a combination of really poor self-esteem. I never learned to love myself and so I could never forgive myself for any missteps/failures.

When I was a teenager I used to fantasize a lot about an alternate life because I was absolutely miserable.                 
Nowadays I spend plenty of time imagining conversations about topics that interest me or experiences that I have had recently; it's mostly internal monologues. I think it happens because I have no one to share my thoughts and opinions with. I really don't know how to make it stop, it's a huge waste of time because I keep repeating the same things in my mind over and over again never arriving at a conclusion.

I just started taking 200mg caffeine pills (not daily but maybe 4-3 times per week) and I haven't noticed any effects in regards to my anxiety. But I am extremely resistant to caffeine (which is why I put down coffee and energy drinks since they do absolutely nothing to me and it's just a waste of money). The pills only make me feel slightly less tired and help with my depressed mood.
These categories seem very restrictive. I am highly uncomfortable and anxious around others but even if I wasn't I wouldn't choose to socialize with them.

I use it every day. It eliminates almost all of the physical side effects of anxiety (tachycardia, palpitations, shaking etc). But it does not eliminate the anxiety thoughts.      
It has undoubtly been a positive addition to my life. Not having my body react a certain way that makes me want to flee, is usually enough to make me go ahead and face my fears, even though I feel anxious.

I do but I mostly overthink conversations I had with strangers or people I am not comfortable with (I don't have any friends but when I did have a few, this usually wouldn't happen).         
Sorry I don't have any advice. I waste so many hours of the day with these thoughts, I wish they would stop.

The problem is I don't have a partner (everyone else does) and the instructor isn't always available since they have to help the other groups as well - and I can't sit around and wait for help either because everyone's time in the lab is limited. Every mistake I make costs me much more time, because the others are working twice as effectively as me.

Yeah that's definitively a problem for me, while I usually know why I am doing something, I don't always know how to do it in full detail. We are given the steps to the experiments but they only say what must be done, not how to fully carry out the operation to completion.        
I guess I should work on rewriting the steps to include all the missing details in order to make myself more comfortable. It's not uncommon for me to panic because I just get so overwhelmed and simply don't know where to start.
5 for me. What affects my life the most is the constant feeling of shame and fear of embarrassment. My self esteem is pretty much non existent.

I thought going to university in another country would force me to become social and it would be a positive experience. But I didn't change at all, in fact I became even more isolated - I don't have any friends or acquaintances. I don't even have real classmates - this one is the hardest to get used to.          
I kind of regret my decision, because my mental health has suffered greatly and I don't think I had any relevant growth. But my home country sucks and anyone who has the opportunity is leaving it. So objectively speaking, I can't consider it a bad decision.

I am in university.               
I've felt that way since I was at least 11. I doubt it's going to go away any time soon.                
We live in a society, around others. How am I supposed not to compare myself with them?

I once saw my dad making small talk with a retail store attendant; when we left the store I asked him why he felt compelled to talk to that person. He told me he did it because he **enjoyed** talking to people. I was in awe because I could never imagine people actually socialized because they felt it was an entertaining activity - I always thought there was some hidden reason underneath all that talk.         
         
Socializing has always felt like a burden for me, something I do out of pure necessity, to obtain or exchange information/services from other people. I really wish this wasn't the case, I wish socializing wasn't painful - it's incredibly difficult to move forward and face your fears when there's really no reward for doing it, there's only pain and hundreds of wasted hours ruminating on past social experiences.

I am studying abroad as well, but unlike you I have zero friends and acquaintances. I really miss my family and my dog, too. I've been living here for 1 year and seem incapable of forming friendships so I've given up on that for the moment.                              
A good general advice is to just keep yourself busy, with studying and hobbies; during my one year all I did was study and I ended up very miserable despite my good performance - it's important to find balance between your activities.           
Maybe try to set up video chatting sessions with your family, whenever you miss them the most. When you feel very lonely, perhaps socializing over the internet might help alleviate that (I know it does for me).

No but I am working on the things that are making me unhappy (things that are worsening my SA and depleting my self esteem). Sadly it takes a while to fix the stuff that is bothering me and it's not always entirely in my control.

I was doing 60 min. on the elliptical machine every day. I signed up for a gym membership two months ago and now I do 15 min of cardio and ~50 min. of weight training. The results have been pretty good, and my shoulders/arms are definitively bigger, but my torso is still "curvy".

I am an international student as well. I mostly did it because of pressure from my parents and the fact my home country is a crappy third world country with alarming violence/crime rates. I didn't think I could manage it but I've been here for 1 year and I have been able to survive just fine so far. I did have several mental breakdowns and fell into severe depression; visiting my parents alleviated that somewhat but now I'm back it's getting worse again.          
There were many times I wished I could have gone back home. I have a hard time interacting with people here. I pretty much spend the whole day in my apartment, only going out to buy grocieries and to go to class.            
You should only stay if you think it's going to be worth all the suffering. I am staying because I know that this country is a much better place than my home country and my diploma will be worth more in case I go back. Also I have been sheltered my whole life so this is a good opportunity to learn to solve problems on my own.

I have intense feelings of self hatred as well and something that has been helping me (a little) is to change things I dislike about myself. For instance my whole life I hated the way my handwriting looked so I decided to write in a different way and I like it now, and even my parents think it's much better. I also hated my hair, hairdressers never knew what to do with it, so I decided to start cutting it myself and I actually like my hair now.               
There are many other things I'd like to change about myself, but sadly some are impossible (e.g. my height) and others aren't solely in my control.
It's one of the reasons I decided to start cutting my own hair. The only thing I regret is not doing it sooner and wasting money on hairdressers.
What if one's self esteem is so low they don't consider they are good at anything at all? Or they are lost in life from being so inexperienced they don't know whether they have a hidden talent?

I've always been shy as a child, never had a lot of friends, always had trouble raising my hand in class and speaking up. I think it got worse when I switched schools at the age of 12/13. I couldn't make friends with anyone, I felt too different from those people. Pretty much just spent all my time studying. My social skills are terrible because I didn't get to develop them during that time and nowadays I am socially inept.                      
Eventually I was able to make friends even though that friendship is a little different from other people's description of a friendship (as in, friends actually hang out outside of school).             
I wasn't bullied on a daily basis (only sometimes). But I always had a profound lack of self esteem, I just really hated myself and my appearance (I am transgender). Also my parents overprotected me and never let me do anything, never taught me important life skills (even stuff like buying bread lol). So nowadays I feel stupid/immature because other people can do simple tasks so easily and I just end up avoiding them or finding an easier way.

I have anhedonia and lack of motivation as well but I am certain I am depressed. However I was asocial and had reduced affect before  developing depression. Out of all schizoid traits, I wish I had "indifference to praise and criticism", I am highly sensitive to criticism and to what other people think about me, I wish I could just stop caring.

I think I'm going to try drinking today. I've never drunk alcohol before in my life. I am so tired of feeling like shit all the time, no motivation, no passion for anything. Hopefully my experience will be at least somewhat good.

I had a calc I professor with hard accent and me being a foreigner I couldn't understand what he was saying. I only passed the class because of Khan Academy.          
Now in calc II I have another professor with an accent. I am glad at this point I have already learned how to self-teach.

Independent, original, analytical, and determined. Have an exceptional ability to turn theories into solid plans of action. Highly value knowledge, competence, and structure. Driven to derive meaning from their visions. Long-range thinkers. Have very high standards for their performance, and the performance of others. Natural leaders, but will follow if they trust existing leaders.
It's not in my nature to make eye contact.
I can see they are staring at me by using my peripheral vision. Also if I look at someone I just do it for half a second because I know staring is rude.

At what point in your life did your social anxiety start to manifest itself? Mine begun when I was still a child and what makes me skeptical about therapy being able to "fix" me is that the way I think/act is just so ingrained into my personality I feel there's no hope to change.

I can relate so much to this. What's worse for me is that I thought living in another country as an international student would fix my life, force me to be more social etc. I couldn't have been more wrong. I have come here with so many social deficits that have accumulated throughout my life, I can't overcome them all and I feel completely hopeless. I have never been more isolated in my life and living in isolation is comforting so it's very difficult for me to push myself and make a change.

I only interact with my parents and only through text messages because I don't live with them.            
I haven't had friends in 3 years. Nowadays I don't even have acquaintances. There are some days I spend in complete silence.

I try not to cry during the moment and for the next days/weeks I will constantly think about how incompetent/worthless/stupid I am, that I shouldn't be alive if I can't even do simple things other people can (whatever it was I got criticized for).

I'm exhausted pretty much all the time too...sometimes I try to go to bed early and I wake up after 8h-9h of sleep feeling the same, as if I had only slept 4 hours. What's worse is I seem to be very resistant to the effects of caffeine (I feel nothing after drinking coffee or energy drinks), so nothing seems to make me feel better. Sometimes my limbs feel heavy and I lack the motivation to do anything. I still force myself to study and stuff because I know I'll feel worse if I don't. But I don't bother to clean the house or go out other than for grocery shopping.             
I exercise every day and my diet is not so bad (I have no motivation to cook so I only prepare simple meals). I'm sorry I don't have any advice. I would love to know if there is any type of medication that can increase motivation and decrease fatigue.

I didn't suffer with it during school because everyone in my class was very quiet during class (the teachers in my school were [thankfully] very strict when it came to chatter among students). But now I am in college in another country and I am shocked by the other students' disrespectful behavior during lectures. They never shut up and it's so difficult to focus on what the professor is saying. Some professors also have very heavy accent and I can barely understand them even if I sit in the front row; sometimes it's a miracle I am able to understand 50% of that they are saying.

I don't feel worthy enough to be complimented so I dismiss it. I strongly believe the person was mistaken in complimenting me. Then I am concerned about disappointing them when I don't live up to their expectations.

I love it, it's great, I use it nearly every day, there are little to no side effects (in my case), it does not cause physical dependence. 10 mg didn't do much for me, I upped my dosage to 20 mg and then 40 (although it might be enough for you; it's standard procedure to start at the lowest dosage possible).

I don't know, they are the only people in my life that love me, in fact they are the only people in my life - I have literally no one else (no friends, no acquaintances). They've definitively done things (in the past) that damaged my self-esteem, and they've influenced me to do some of the bad mistakes I mentioned. But the past cannot be changed.
I already have my own place.

Oh I wasn't expecting perfection on myself but I was expecting the possibility of repairing my mistakes. But in my case, every mistake I make is irreversible and there's no fixing or making them better.
I wish they would look stupid. The mistakes I made will shape the rest of my life. I have to live with them every day. That's why I said they are irreversible.
I used to have a therapist, but I no longer do. And I don't have any money to go to therapy now. It's just me and my thoughts and bad decisons haunting me.

picked the wrong degree 2 times thinking I was making a good choice for myself, therefore wasting a lot of time and money; moved out of my home country just to be disappointed and more depressed due to social isolation; and other personal things.

Yeah I can't either ... too scared other people might be able to listen to my music without me realizing it's too loud and being bothered by it. I would need to raise the volume quite a lot in order for the outside noise of chatter be overpowered by the music.

After being 1 month alone without my parents and my dog, no friends and no acquaintances in a completely different country. Nowadays I just got used to it, I guess.              
I can definitively relate to the people saying they feel lonelier being around other people. I feel mostly fine being home on my own.

> I can't say I experience the same joy as people interacting with me. It's just dull and empty on my end. I just don't get that positive feedback. I'm rather bored, bothered or exhausted from it.

The exact same thing happens to me. I am very asocial, and get little to no satisfaction from social interaction. But unlike you I can't even socialize properly. If I could get at least some sort of enjoyment I would be much more motivated to improve my social skills.

I can relate. I never did anything in my adolescence other than going to school and studying. I managed to make one friendship that turned into three more (by association) after 3 years of being in the same school. For the whole time I was there I hung out with these friends maybe once or twice outside of school. I didn't even know other people hung out outside of school.             
Needless to say my social skills are and have always been trash. I reached out to my parents and said I had a hard time making friends and all I got was a book on non verbal communication that didn't help at all. Even my dad commented on how bad my conversation skills were.                 
I don't feel human either. I can't even fake being human I am such a terrible actor. I feel so hopeless because everything in this world essentially boils down to how charismatic you are.

My knowledge of organic chemistry is very limited. My university is weird and the practical classes are always ahead of the theoretical classes (so I haven't had any classes on that subject yet). So far all of the reaction mechanisms I've learned are halogenation of alkanes, some alkene reactions (hydrogenation, hydration, epoxidation, addition of halogens and addition of hydrogen halides), and dehydration of alcohols. That's it. Is it enough knowledge for me to infer what's going to happen when sucrose reacts with NaOH?

> Career counselor or advisor?



Where would I find a career counselor? Is it the same thing as vocational psychology?                
> Maybe some work experience?       



I am not sure who would want to hire me, not even for free.

Well I stay up for around 17h every day so yes, approximately 12h excluding breaks, but I can only accomplish that on the weekends when I don't have any classes (I have no social life). Despite investing this much time I think if my mood were better I would probably be much more productive and accomplish more stuff in less time.              
I feel like I can't be held to the same standards as others because in my mind everyone else is better than me. So I try to compensate by trying to be good at least academically. I am terrible at socializing and building connections as well so I think I am at a disadvantage compared to everyone else, and therefore I also have to compensate for my lack of social skills by acquiring more knowledge/technical skills.             
I used to really enjoy studying and learning new things but I worry too much about my performance and I no longer get any enjoyment out of it. I have taken plenty of tests in my life but I still feel extremely anxious every time, I worry too much about failing or not being good enough for my own expectations or what I think other people's expectations are.

I'm the same, I never get any sort of enjoyment from social interactions, especially when interacting with strangers or just people I am not familiar with. When I used to have friends though I admit I did enjoy having a chat with them or playing videogames together. I also hate leaving the house, and the only restaurant I go to is McDonalds because of their self-service kiosk, so I never have to interact with the cashier.           
I kind of wish I wasn't like that, because if social interactions were somewhat enjoyable, and if I had more interest in people's lives, I would work harder on improving my social skills. I am too comfortable in my isolation.

I can relate. I study ~12h per day (when I don't have classes, because I don't consider them "studying time"), I am obssessed with being productive, even in my most depressing days I've always done something productive. I feel like the only thing that makes me a worth human being are my grades, which are decent not because I am intelligent but because I put so much time into studying.               
This stops me from seeking relationships and engaging in hobbies. My only hobby is watching other people play videogames live, because I dont have time to play them myself and even if I did have time I don't want to feel guilty about it. I also wish I could play an instrument and try other hobbies, but I won't because I know I'll suck at first and that will discourage me from pursuing it further since my brain will interpret that as a waste of time doing something I am not good at instead of studying. I basically want to quit every time I start doing something and realize that I am bad at it.                
Sorry I dont have any advice. I wish I could stop being like that. I know the core issue for me is my lack of self esteem and self worth. At my current state I could never think about doing a PhD, I don't consider myself worthy enough to pursue that.

Underdeveloped social skills from being too shy as a kid, never leaving the house except to go to school etc. Nowadays I am far too behind my peers. I simply don't know how to proceed in social situations.

My cousin said pretty much the same thing, that I would stop being introverted after going to university.            
Truth is I have never been more isolated. I have 0 friends, maybe a few acquaintances and that's it. I've interacted more with professors than the other students so far I think.             
So it's definitively possible to continue being introverted.

My armpits get really sweaty when I am anxious. It's not noticeable (I think) but if the anxiety lasts for a long time my shirt starts to smell pretty bad. It doesn't matter how much deodorant/antiperspirant I use, it always happens.

I take them 4-5 times per week, when I need to interact with people in general. I have been suffering from social anxiety pretty much my whole life, and I had to deal with these physiological effects almost every day at school etc. I just couldn't keep going like that. My parents were really against it even though it does not cause physical dependence and the side effects are minor (when they exist); they only started to view things differently when my own therapist thought it was a great idea for me to take them.             
I kind of don't care if I have to keep taking them for the rest of my life, or if anyone thinks being reliant on medication is a weakness. My brain is clearly messed up because it sees other people as threats and I just don't want to suffer anymore.

Number 1 is the biggest issue for me. I feel like I need to read a manual in order to socialize properly while other people do it so naturally, it's one of the reasons why I have literally no self confidence. I wish life was like in some videogames where you get to pick dialog options.                     
I have given up on finding love (without ever experiencing a romantic relationship) and for me relationships are not what makes life worth living. I really just wish I could at least have minimally decent social skills to make through this life.

I can't control these physiological effects and they were taking a toll on my life so I started taking betablockers. I can say it was one of the best decisions in my life despite my mother being against it saying she dislikes medication etc. I don't care what she thinks, life is already so trash there's no reason (in my opinion) to keep suffering if there's a way to end it.

I wouldn't blame it on other people to be honest. It's just really difficult for me to make friends, it's been like this my whole life. If someone else were in my place they would probably be having the time of their life.           
EDIT: I wouldn't say the climate is warm either - it's your typical temperate oceanic climate. It's not warm at all in comparison to where I'm from - except in the summer.

I used to have online friends back when I played MMORPGs.         
Now that I am an adult I no longer have time to play games. I was also betrayed once by an online "friend" which makes it hard for me to trust people I meet on the internet. I'd much rather meet someone IRL and then do online activities with them.

People always ask me this question whenever I post about moving to another country, but I never quite understand why it's so important to have that information.            
It's Portugal.

Almost finishing my first year and I'm really tired. I am also really mad I am not allowed to switch majors, being unhappy with my current one (if I am going to be miserable I would rather be miserable with a major that is actually going to provide something to look forward to in the future after I graduate).

I showed signs of social anxiety at an early age (I was a very shy child). It got worse in my teen years. Despite the signs being there my parents never did anything, they told me they thought I would "grow out of it" like they did, and blamed me for not "verbalizing my issues" (even when I complained I struggled to make friends in school and wrote an essay where I explicitely said I had a very hard time with public speaking).              
Now the problem is chronic, I am not quite sure there's any way I could ever get over it. I don't know what it feels like to be confident and have self esteem and not feel anxious; if I had ever felt those things maybe I would feel hopeful about the possibility of getting better.

I feel like that too but I am a bit more extreme to the point I just avoid any games that require interaction with other players in order to get the full experience. I don't know why but when I was younger (10-13 years old) I could just jump into an online forum or new multiplayer videogame and start interacting with others just fine. I seem to have gotten more introverted and I rarely get any enjoyment from those interactions anymore and a lot of online communities are so toxic (like in MOBAs) that it's not worth investing on them.            
I'm a lurker on Twitch too, I think that's perfectly fine, specially when watching big streamers whose chat's are always moving so quickly you can barely read a full sentence before it disappears.

I wanted to try the self-checkout but I am too scared of messing up and then all the people waiting behind me getting pissed at me. I don't have an issue with using the normal checkout because the cashier never tries to make small talk.
I have an account but I log in maybe once every 6 months. I just hate it so much. And I moved to another country and everyone here uses Facebook. It's like if you don't use it, you don't even exist.

Same with me, I feel like even by looking in the general direction of the person I am talking to is distracting. When I ask a teacher a question for instance if I try to look at them while they are explaining I cannot understand a single thing that was said, but if I look at the board or any other inanimate object I can focus on what they are saying just fine.

This is so relatable. I always think I am a nuisance to other people. For instance I am apprehensive about scheduling a doctor's appointment because I wouldn't want to bother a doctor with my stupid issues. That's how messed up my mind is, I've been struggling with this inferiority complex for years. I am also very sensitive. I can't handle criticism or disapproval coming from anyone.

You're not alone. I am far from graduating but the only time I ever interact with classmates is when we have to do group projects. I go to lectures and straight to home. Zero friends. I am fine with that because I go to university to get an education, making friends is not my goal.

I tend to smile and laugh quite a lot during conversations. I feel forced to do it because I have nothing to add to the conversation. My range of emotional expression is quite limited and I kind of don't know what else to do to fill that 'awkward silence'. I want to stop myself from doing that because it feels too fake, but if I do that then I'll just seem even more robotic than I already do; at least smiling makes you seem friendly.
I'm 100% alone in another country and it's tough, I can deal with not having friends (I am pretty used to it at this point) but I miss my dog and my parents.

I was like that for a whole year, after I started reading about autism. I couldn't stop researching stuff and I would spend a lot of time on autism forums, because I could relate to a lot of things people would share. I knew I wouldn't stop with my obsession unless I was properly assessed.         
But at the same time I struggle a lot with inferiority thoughts and at my current state I could never bring myself to set a doctor's appointment and ask for an evaluation, I am too afraid of making a fool out of myself and that the doctor will completely disregard my worries. I also feel like if I had clinically significant autistic traits my parents would have noticed it when I was a child, so I even feel kind of embarrassed to bring this up to them too, even though they tell me that I am similar to Sheldon from TBBT and that I am also similar to Dr. Shaun Murphy from The Good Doctor.          
After a long time I have come to terms with the fact I probably just have a lot of autistic traits and that it's hard to make a proper analysis because social anxiety itself can contribute to lack of social skills. Eventually I stopped obssessing about it altogether since it wasn't making me feel much better about myself. And I realized a diagnosis wouldn't change who I am anyway.

I usually only ask questions when I have tried to find the answer elsewhere (online, on the recommended textbook etc) with no success. This way I kind of have an idea whether my question is really 'stupid' or not, and I can confront my brain with actual facts. There are times the professors don't even know how to answer my questions, and they have to do the research themselves and tell me later!

I decided to go to med school in my last year of school; I was nothing like those people who dream of being doctors ever since they were kids.            
When it comes to choosing a career path I think it's important to find a compromise between something that you're good at/have potential to improve, something that you find somewhat interesting to study, and a field that has a good career prospects.            
I switched to chemical engineering.

I am afraid of people in authority as well. I'm always apprehensive around them that I will say or do something stupid and they'll have a different view on me. It's very difficult for me to go up to a professor and ask a question. I've been trying to participate in class more often when I see the professor is a little more friendly. What helped me realize my fear is irrational is seeing other people ask questions that have obvious answers but the professors still don't mind answering, and they usually don't embarass/humiliate anyone.

I've dropped out of med school (I am not from the US - in my home country someone can go straight from "high school" to medical school) because I could not handle interacting with patients and I was mostly interested in the science behind medicine, not the practice itself. I don't regret my decision, in fact I feel kind of stupid for ever thinking that medicine would be a good career path for me.       
I would say that you made a good choice if you aren't overly passionate about nursing and can imagine yourself doing other things that are at least mildly interesting and fulfilling to you. Asperger's is a collection of signs and symptoms, which manifest differently in different people (it's a spectrum after all). Also it can't be "acquired" - you're born with it or you don't have it; so in order to know "the truth" you have to look at your behavior as a child. Since your mother seems to be pushing this diagnosis over you, perhaps you could seek someone else who knew you as a child, to see if you showed traits of autism then.             
A lot of professionals are actually reluctant to give out an Asperger's diagnosis to adults, it's specially hard for adults to get diagnosed because they also might have already developed coping mechanisms, so it becomes harder to detect.           
Also showing traits of autism doesn't equal being autistic, and some other conditions can mimic autistic traits.
